old: When characterizing towns and people, choose the appropriate relative pronoun: *aki* (referring to people), *ami* (referring to whole clauses or indefinite concepts), *amely* (formal relative pronoun referring to specific things/places), and *amelyik* (selecting one specific item from a set).
new: You know *aki* (who: for people), *ami* and *amely* (which, that: for things) from A2 Unit 4. *Ami* can also point back to a whole clause: *Sok bolt van a városban, ami nagyon kényelmes.* (There are many shops in the town, which is very convenient.)

old: Relative pronouns take case endings depending on their grammatical function in the subordinate clause: *akinek* (dative: to whom / whose), *amelyben* (inessive: in which), *amiről* (delative: about which), *ahová* (lative: whereto).
new: The relative word takes the ending that its own clause needs: *a bolt, amelyben dolgozom* (I work in it: -ban/-ben), *a könyv, amiről beszélünk* (we talk about it: -ról/-ről), *a tanár, akinek segítek* (I help him or her: -nak/-nek), *a város, ahová megyünk* (we are going to it).

old: The derivational suffix *-beli* forms adjectives denoting location or belonging: *környékbeli* (local, from the surrounding area), *városbeli* (townsperson / urban), *falubeli* (fellow villager), *helybeli* (local resident).
new: The ending *-beli* turns a place word into an adjective meaning 'from that place': *falu* -> *falubeli* (from the village), *város* -> *városbeli* (from the town), *hely* -> *helybeli* (local), *környék* -> *környékbeli* (from the neighbourhood). The adjective does not change: *a falubeli emberek*. Used as a noun it takes *-ek*: *a falubeliek* (the villagers).

old: To balance differing lifestyles, use contrastive conjunctions and transitional adverbs: *míg* (while / whereas), *ellenben* (on the other hand), *ezzel szemben* (in contrast to this), and *ugyanakkor* (at the same time).
new: To contrast two facts, Hungarian uses *azonban* (however), *viszont* (on the other hand) and *ezzel szemben* (in contrast to this). *Azonban* and *viszont* can stand after the first word or phrase of the second sentence; *ezzel szemben* usually opens it. You know *míg* (while, whereas) from Unit 4 for a contrast inside one sentence.
